quotes.text: The harmonised definition of the household response unit is “one person living alone or a group of people (not necessarily related) living at the same address who share cooking facilities and share a living room or sitting room or dining area. The LFS definition differs slightly. The LFS adds students who live in halls of residence in term-time and residents in National Health Service accommodation to the coverage allowed in the harmonised definition, but these are clearly identified and the harmonised definition can be derived.
Family: DVs created for each family on the database; on a flat file each family member would carry the same value for each family based DV;
quotes.location: SECTION 6 - CODING AND PROCESSING THE DATA, 6.2 DERIVED VARIABLES, p. 51

quotes.text: The following primary topics are not included on the LFS : Agency workers, Carers and Mobile Phone use.

assessments.reasoning:
The assessment of each element is as follows:
- member_to_member_relationships: False. Although the text mentions a 'relationship grid' and 'Relationship to HRP', it does not establish that relationships are collected member-to-member (matrix/triangular grid) rather than relative to the Household Reference Person.
- extended_ties: False. The text does not enumerate the relationship categories to substantiate whether ties beyond spouse and parent-child (such as grandparent-grandchild, siblings, non-kin) can be identified.
- multiple_household_criteria: True. Note (i) to Table 15.1 explicitly states the criteria for defining and separating household response units (sharing cooking facilities, sharing a living room/sitting room/dining area, or resident in student/NHS accommodation).
- sub_units: True. Section 6.2 and Section 6.3 confirm that family-level sub-units are identified and assigned within households via family-based derived variables (DVs) and relationship checks.
- caregiving_relationships: False. Table 15.1 explicitly states that 'Carers' are not included in the LFS.
